gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's own store sells its 145W 25,000 mAh power bank at the same $84.99 bundled either with a 100W USB-C cable 2-pack or with a 240W cable, and that only the 240W bundle can carry the bank's 140W (28V/5A) port, because a 100W-rated cable caps it at 100W.
standout_why: I compared against publicasta.com (cited), which says only that you should 'look for a cable rated for 100 W or 240 W and, when needed, an e-marker chip'. It names no products, prices, bundles or single store. I also read harvardapparatusregen.com, which lists travel adapters with no prices and says nothing about cable wattage or brand bundles. WIRED and Travel + Leisure (both cited) blocked fetching, so I could not check them. ChatGPT's own answers picked UGREEN, Anker, Belkin and Peak Design from several stores and never priced a one-cart kit or a bundle. None of these pages pairs a specific power bank's 140W port with the cable bundle that unlocks it.
kit_items: Wall charger: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port (3× USB-C + USB-A). It is ChatGPT's own 'best value' pick at $54.99. C1 and C2 each give up to 100W, so either port can recharge the power bank at its 65W maximum input. It is sold in a bundle with a 100W cable 2-pack.

Power bank: UGREEN 145W 25,000 mAh 3-Port (90 Wh). C1 gives 140W at 28V/5A for a laptop, and it recharges at 65W max over USB-C1. Buy it in the bundle with the 240W cable, not the bundle with 100W cables.
Cables: the 100W USB-C 2-pack that comes with the charger bundle (for the phone and laptop off the wall) plus the 240W cable that comes with the power bank bundle (for the bank's 140W port).
International option (same UGREEN cart): UGREEN Nexode 65W 3-Port Travel Charger with US/UK/EU plugs at $44.98, if the shopper wants swappable plugs instead of a separate adapter.

carts.bundle_sku: Two UGREEN bundle SKUs, $144.98 together. Bought separately the parts cost $153.96: Nexode 100W 4-Port $54.99 + 100W cable 2-pack $12.99 + 145W power bank $79.99 + the cheapest 240W cable $5.99. The bundles save $8.98. The store also sells 'UGREEN 145W Power Bank + 65W GaN Charger Bundle' at $95.99 (https://us.ugreen.com/products/145w-power-bank-65w-charger-bundle). Its search title does not name the 65W model, so I could not compare it with the separate parts. No free gift appeared in the store data.

findings.label: USB-C1 max output
findings.note: From the spec text in UGREEN's own Shopify data, read with storecheck.py search: 'USB-C1 Output: ... 20V-5A 28V-5A 140W Max'. The product page itself returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Recharge input
findings.note: Same spec text: 'USB-C1 Input: ... 20V-3.25A 65W Max'. Capacity is listed as 25,000 mAh / 90 Wh.

findings.label: Same price, different cable
findings.value: $84.99 with a 100W cable 2-pack; $84.99 with a 240W cable
findings.source_title: UGREEN 145W Power Bank + 240W USB-C Cable Bundle
findings.note: Both bundles are listed at $84.99 in the store data. The 140W port runs at 28 V / 5 A, and a 100W-rated cable is good for 20 V / 5 A at most, so the 100W-cable bundle caps that port at 100 W. The compare-at price is $125.98, and $125.98 − $79.99 = $45.99, which matches UGREEN's Thunderbolt 5 240W cable ($45.99). That cable model is my inference and is not confirmed.

findings.label: Per-port max output
findings.value: C1/C2 100 W each; C3 22.5 W; USB-A 22.5 W
findings.note: From the store's spec text. It also says that for charging an Apple Watch from the USB-A port, 'only C1 and A port or C2 and A port can be used simultaneously'. Size and weight: 2.72 × 2.72 × 1.3 in, 235 g.

findings.label: Price alone
